newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India settles for end-week,-month,-year.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India settles for end-week,-month,-year.

text.p: Indian GDRs started the day with a small rally after some good results but subsided into lacklustre trade ahead of the weekend, the end of the month and the slower Christmas holiday season ahead.
"There were some good results earlier -- from State Bank of India yesterday, and the market ran away with itself a little," said one trader.
"But then India Aluminium figures came out 21 percent lower and the market slowed up. It was very quiet towards the end of the day."

At 1300 GMT the Cazenove Indian GDR Index was 0.68 points or 1.02 percent up at 67.09 after the Bombay Stock Exchange 30 share index ended 23.66 points or 0.82 percent higher at a provisional 2,894.68.
The premium for GDRs over stocks on the local market was 18.50 percent after 17.93 percent on Thursday.
Towards the end of the day Grasim, Indian Hotels, Hindalco, Bajaj Auto and ITC were all up from Thursday's close but Reliance and Mahindra were slightly down, and Tata was flat at $10.0.
Elsewhere new issue Solidere was at $11.75, up 0.15 on the day, traders said. It was launched this week at $11.50.
Next week, activity is expected to be even less with few results left this year and the usual December slow-down.
"In fact the Indian market hasn't been very exciting in the last few weeks, although it is very cheap," said a trader.
"There will be two main forces next week. There are still some bottom-fishers around but you have to balance that element against the seasonal effect."
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI was at 59.57 at 1600 GMT, up 0.16 or 0.27 percent, with a premium of 20.95 percent.
Capel's Korea GDR Index was at 65.83, down 0.27 or 0.41 percent, with a premium of 28.80 percent from 29.42 percent over the local market yesterday.
The Taiwan Index was up down 1.75 or 1.85 percent., with a premium of 4.50 percent from 4.82 percent on Thursday. -- London newsroom 44 171 542 5887
